query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled 5 vol% nano-dispersion of tungsten oxide into the CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy will stabilize and lower the friction coefficient and wear rate from room temperature to 800 °C compared to the unmodified alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix without any nano-dispersion
generation.intervention: Incorporate ~5 vol% tungsten oxide nanoparticles during the alloy processing stage to achieve a uniform nano-dispersion in the matrix
generation.conditions: Pin-on-disk sliding tests conducted in ambient air over a temperature range from room temperature to 800 °C under varying loads that simulate typical operating conditions
generation.structural_mediator: A homogeneous dispersion of tungsten oxide particles throughout the alloy, which acts as nucleation sites for a lubricious tribofilm
generation.mechanism: The tungsten oxide particles are expected to facilitate the formation of a stable, self-lubricating oxide layer during sliding. This layer minimizes direct metal-to-metal contact and adapts to temperature-induced oxidation changes, thereby reducing frictional shear and mitigating wear. At high temperatures, the inherent lubricious nature of tungsten oxide should help maintain a low friction coefficient, while at lower temperatures its presence reinforces the matrix against wear.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline CoCrFeNi alloy, the tungsten oxide–modified alloy should exhibit a consistently lower and less fluctuating friction coefficient and a reduced wear rate throughout the full temperature range, including under increased load conditions.
generation.baseline: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy without tungsten oxide dispersion, which shows high variability in friction and wear properties across the temperature range due to dynamic tribo-oxidation and adhesion effects
generation.boundary: The expected benefits hold true under controlled ambient air conditions, moderate to high sliding loads, and over temperatures from room temperature up to 800 °C. Deviations in environment (e.g., inert atmospheres), excessively high loads, or poor dispersion of tungsten oxide may alter performance.
generation.uncertainty: While tungsten oxide is known for its lubricious behavior at elevated temperatures, the precise quantitative impact on friction and wear in a CoCrFeNi matrix remains to be determined. Factors such as the uniformity of the dispersion and interfacial bonding between tungsten oxide and the matrix could significantly influence the overall performance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of plain CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy and another set modified with a 5 vol% tungsten oxide nano-dispersion. Subject both sets to pin-on-disk sliding tests in ambient air while varying temperature from room temperature to 800 °C and adjusting the applied load to simulate different operating conditions.
measurements: Record the coefficient of friction at different temperatures and loads using in situ sensors
Quantify wear rate via weight loss measurements and surface profilometry after tests
Characterize the worn surface and tribofilm using SEM/TEM to assess film continuity and composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the tungsten oxide modified samples do not show a statistically significant improvement (i.e., a consistently lower and more stable friction coefficient along with reduced wear rates across the full temperature range) compared to the unmodified baseline, or if the tribofilm does not form as predicted, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.kind: web:4.2. Effect of Nano-Al2O3 on Wear Performance
cited_evidence.text: The appropriate addition of nano-Al2O3 particles can effectively suppress surface oxidation caused by frictional heat through grain refinement and enhanced the matrix strength. The main component (1 wt% Al2O3) was retained as shown by the improvement in TEM and mechanical properties. The wear surface composition reflects dynamic wear processes (e.g., trioxidation reactions, particle removal, and matrix smearing), and localized Al and O signals were reduced despite the addition of Al2O3. The small difference in Al (0.2%) is within the uncertainty of the EDS, whereas the larger reduction in O is attributed to the dominant role of matrix-derived oxides, as well as the loss of Al2O3 particles during wear and the inaccuracy of lightweight elements in the EDS. Frictional contact generates localized temperatures exceeding 300–500 °C. These elevated temperatures promote the dissociation of oxygen molecules and chemisorption on active metal sites (Fe, Cr). The adsorbed oxygen then reacts with metal atoms, forming oxide nuclei (e.g., FeO, Cr2O3).
